title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 0.4 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sheet formability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ion-conductive solid in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In the monoclinic structure, indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LATP material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. With germanium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a niobium oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 60 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyacrylonitrile based electrolyte of 50 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The roll pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding vinylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises nickel sulfide impregnated in carbon nanotubes and a carbon coating on the composite. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The confinement of nickel sulfide in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3YCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which iron sulfide is confined in the pores of porous carbon to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. A separator coated with porous carbon traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising iron sulfide, porous carbon, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the iron sulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 75 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the moisture stability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.01 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Amperometric carbon dioxide sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 500 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the lanthanum strontium manganite sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of carbon dioxide concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to carbon dioxide against interfering gases. The protective layer improves the durability of the NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate sensor in an exhaust gas.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a solid electrolyte layer. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 75 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 50 mPa s to 2500 mPa s.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and LLTO material. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The resulting Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

assignee: University Of Selexen INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC Cooperation Foundation
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1.
