The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The capacity retention of 88% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%.

title: Multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor with improved heat resistance at 125 degrees C
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The capacitor withstands 125 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the aluminum capacitor. A power module combining the capacitor with a lithium battery is also described. The dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) gives a uniform polymer layer and a high capacitance appearance rate for the 220 microfarad rating.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of aluminum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) doped with naphthalenesulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 15 milliohms or less.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY Co., Ltd.
title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute Of Energy Materials
title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, LiF, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Tin-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 5 V
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The resulting Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The 1.2 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The additive vinylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. The LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state battery. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 93% or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more.

title: Composite cathode comprising iron sulfide and porous carbon and lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a iron sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The porous carbon framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of iron sulfide. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 100 cycles is also described. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. Polysulfide dissolution from the iron sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; iron sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing vinylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The additive vinylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The capacity retention of 88% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive lithium difluorophosphate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. With 3 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

assignee: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene based electrolyte of 50 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance and sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.3 MPa or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 40% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The content of GeS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LATP and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The content of SiS2 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1.
