A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 and LiF material. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The roll pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The resulting LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. With 0.5 wt% of 1,3-propane sultone, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The additive 1,3-propane sultone is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using tetrahydrofuran and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The membrane of 100 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 60 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability and moisture stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and SiS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix, lithium perchlorate as the lithium salt, and tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether as a plasticizer. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The sheet thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, the porosity is 10% or less, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A precursor of the Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF, Li3YCl6, and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. With zirconium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, zirconium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes for lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The LATP and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the high-voltage stability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The arsenic-free antimony content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A precursor of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: An argyrodite ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature.
