A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

assignee: Qilunhe New Energy Technology CO., LTD.
title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, InCl3, and TiCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium difluorophosphate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 92% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and tin substitution for improved moisture stability
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid is a crystallized glass comprising a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix having a Li2S to P2S5 molar ratio of 75:25 in which 2 mol% to 6 mol% of the phosphorus is substituted by tin, and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated from the matrix. A glassy precursor prepared by melt quenching at 750 degrees C is reheated at 240 degrees C to 280 degrees C so that the beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 100 nm and a degree of crystallinity of 50% to 75%. The tin, a soft acid, binds the sulfur more strongly than phosphorus, and the cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 60 minutes is 8 cm3/g or less. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and retains 80% or more of the conductivity after the exposure. Unlike crystalline Li7P3S11 or Li6PS5Cl powders, the remaining vitreous phase gives good deformability, and an all-solid-state battery using the material shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid which is a crystallized glass comprising: a vitreous phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25, wherein 2 mol% to 6 mol% of phosphorus is substituted by tin; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated from the vitreous phase, wherein a degree of crystallinity determined by X-ray diffraction is 50% to 75%, and a cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 60 minutes is 8 cm3/g or less.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. With zirconium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 84% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 80% or more.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 500 to 650 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 5 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 500 to 650 degrees C is described. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. The solid electrolyte layer of samarium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. A hybrid system in which the fuel cell charges a lithium ion battery is also described. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The thin 5 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The content of GeS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The LiF material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and production method thereof
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The resulting LATP, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The capacity retention of 88% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The resulting Li2ZrO3 and LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of LiI is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The uniaxial pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a lithium sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 2.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 92%. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Composite cathode comprising titanium disulfide and graphene and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The cathode delivering 600 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The titanium disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The titanium disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising titanium disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In the trigonal structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
