An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The uniaxial pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Described is a combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes for lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: nickel sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, carbon nanotubes, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The composite shows a capacity of 1000 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. Polysulfide dissolution from the nickel sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyvinylidene fluoride. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode. The anode support contains nickel oxide and yttria-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 500 to 650 degrees C. The yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The cell can be operated at 500 to 650 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a relative density of 95%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 500 to 650 degrees C. The solid electrolyte of yttria-stabilized zirconia is a dense ceramic of 95% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite on the sintered electrolyte.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The cell retains 92% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 87% or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The viscosity of 3000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material. A precursor of the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 84% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C, and wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming an ion-conductive solid sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Potentiometric ammonia sensor having an auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for ammonia. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The platinum electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of ammonia concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting ammonia, comprising: a ceramic body comprising sodium beta-alumina; a sensing electrode comprising platinum disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 700 degrees C.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, graphene, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. The active material iron sulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The cathode delivering 1000 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising iron sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The warm isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by atomic layer deposition followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V.
