The content of GeS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. With 1 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The content of GeS2 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY IDNUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more.

title: UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyacrylonitrile matrix, lithium perchlorate as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and LATP material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state lithium battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 650 to 800 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a relative density of 95%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 650 to 800 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The anode support contains nickel oxide and lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. The stack of 200 cells can be paired with a lithium battery for load leveling.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 15 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyethylene oxide and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a magnesium additive. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved electrochemical window and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa.

assignee: University Of Selexen INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC Cooperation Foundation
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The LiF material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 45% or more.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The content of GeS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and GeS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Ag-C layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75.

title: Sulfide glass ceramic solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 crystal phase with controlled crystallinity and widened electrochemical window
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte is a glass ceramic in which a Li7P3S11 crystal phase is precipitated in a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix having a Li2S to P2S5 molar ratio of 70:30 and containing LiI in an amount of 3 mol% to 8 mol%. A glass obtained by mechanical amorphization of the raw materials in a planetary mill is heat-treated at 260 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 1 hour to 3 hours, just above the crystallization onset, so that the metastable Li7P3S11 phase precipitates with a crystallite size of 30 nm to 150 nm while devitrification to the low-conductivity Li4P2S6 phase is kept to 3% or less. The degree of crystallinity is 60% to 85%, the residual glassy phase deforms plastically during cold pressing, and the glass ceramic has an ionic conductivity of 4.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C with an activation energy of 0.22 eV. The iodide widens the electrochemical window on the reduction side to 1.6 V versus Li/Li+. The glass ceramic is distinguished from crystalline Li6PS5Cl or Li3PS4 powders by the presence of the vitreous phase and gives an all-solid-state battery with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte which is a glass ceramic comprising: a vitreous phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and LiI in an amount of 3 mol% to 8 mol%; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the vitreous phase, wherein a degree of crystallinity determined by X-ray diffraction is 60% to 85%, a content of a Li4P2S6 phase is 3% or less, and the glass ceramic has an ionic conductivity of 4.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The indium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The Li3YCl6 and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 0.4 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyethylene oxide matrix, lithium hexafluorophosphate as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1.
