A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ion-conductive solid powder with 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing vinylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, vinylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 92% of its capacity after 300 cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 92% with the electrolyte. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 2 wt%. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. With 2 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7% after 100 cycles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The cold isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyacrylonitrile based electrolyte of 50 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The tin content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 45% or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and method for producing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The total ionic conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium bis(oxalato)borate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% with the electrolyte. With 0.5 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The warm isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Mixed potential type hydrogen sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a gold electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the hydrogen concentration. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 700 degrees C. The sensor shows a response time of 2 seconds to a step change of hydrogen concentration at 700 degrees C. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for hydrogen. The sensor with a response time of 2 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for hydrogen. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of hydrogen.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The 1.2 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate is also described. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The capacity retention of 92% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The LATP, LLZO, and LLTO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The LLZO, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 91% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The LiF and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing alumina nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes.
