The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The ion-conductive solid shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li6PS5Cl material. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The high coverage of the coating results in improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The LiPON layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The bilayer structure improves the moisture stability compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The initial capacity of 800 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the molybdenum disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The active material molybdenum disulfide is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The active material is coated with a thin lithium phosphosulfide ion conductor layer so that the cathode can be used in a solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. With 3 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from 1,2-dimethoxyethane, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved sinterability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

assignee: Qilunhe New Energy Technology CO., LTD.
title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The tin substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Described is a combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. With 2 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1150 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 950 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Al2O3 inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

assignee: Qilunhe New Energy Technology CO., LTD.
title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state lithium battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating.
