The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The sulfur cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles is also described. The active material sulfur is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising sulfur, carbon nanotubes, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the sulfur is 2 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyacrylonitrile matrix, lithium hexafluorophosphate as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Tin-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a lithium secondary battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ion-conductive solid in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In the monoclinic structure, indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises iron sulfide impregnated in ketjen black and a carbon coating on the composite. Polysulfide dissolution from the iron sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the iron sulfide cathode. The confinement of iron sulfide in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising iron sulfide, ketjen black, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the iron sulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The material comprises Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C.

title: semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. A precursor of the LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The resulting Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium bis(oxalato)borate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The 1.2 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. With germanium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more.

title: Composite cathode comprising nickel sulfide and ketjen black and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, ketjen black, and carboxymethyl cellulose is described. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising ketjen black; nickel sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The content of Li2O is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. With a binder content of 0.5 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polycarbonate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The cold isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The capacity retention of 85% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The warm isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 2 mA/cm2. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4.
