In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 50 mPa s to 2500 mPa s.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute Of Energy Materials
title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and beta-Li3PS4. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 15 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 700 to 850 degrees C is described. The reversible cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 700 to 850 degrees C. A hybrid system in which the fuel cell charges a lithium ion battery is also described. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode at 700 to 850 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a zinc additive. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The roll pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Mixed potential type nitrogen oxide sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: An exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell, a sensing cell, and a diffusion controlling portion is described. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 400 degrees C. The sensor detects nitrogen oxide with high selectivity and a response time of 2 seconds. The sensor shows a response time of 2 seconds to a step change of nitrogen oxide concentration at 400 degrees C. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The sensing electrode comprises gold and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The multilayer structure with the sodium beta-alumina ceramic allows mass production by co-firing.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects nitrogen oxide.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The uniaxial pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The oxygen substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the cycle life are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of nickel sulfide. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C. Polysulfide dissolution from the nickel sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and carboxymethyl cellulose. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: sulfur positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the sulfur cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. The sulfur is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; sulfur impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The roll pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The LATP and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm.

assignee: Seodam National University INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC Cooperation Foundation
title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The content of GeS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the high-voltage stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%.
