title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. With 1 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 50 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, fluoroethylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The warm isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and beta-Li3PS4. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor with a conductive polymer solid electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a solid electrolytic capacitor element whose leakage current is reduced by a repair step of the dielectric film. The equivalent series resistance is 10 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the niobium capacitor. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The 100 microfarad capacitor smooths the output of a lithium battery converter.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a niobium anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 25 V.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium bromide solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The cold isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9.

title: Hafnium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Method for forming a conductive polymer layer on a dielectric oxide of a solid electrolytic capacitor
abstract: A solid electrolytic capacitor includes a porous aluminum anode body, a dielectric oxide film formed on the anode body, a conductive polymer layer comprising polyaniline doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a carbon layer, and a silver layer. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The 330 microfarad capacitor smooths the output of a lithium battery converter. The capacitor has a capacitance of 330 microfarads, a rated voltage of 25 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 8 milliohms at 100 kHz. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The capacitor rated at 25 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous aluminum anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of polyaniline particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. The LLTO and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The LLTO and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 200 degrees C.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C, and wherein 0.01 <= v <= 0.7.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an oxygen source at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room

A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an oxygen source at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7% after 100 cycles. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
