A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3). In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The LiF, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the sheet formability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfur cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. A lithium-sulfur battery with the sulfur cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The carbon coating on the sulfur composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. The Li3PS4 and LATP material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7P3S11. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 16% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LLZO material. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and HfBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiBr, YBr3, and HfBr4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Composite cathode comprising sulfur and ketjen black and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, ketjen black, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. Polysulfide dissolution from the sulfur cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 5 mg/cm2. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved moisture stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 84% or more, and wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO, LATP, and Li2ZrO3 material. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 950 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 70% or more.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tantalum and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. With zirconium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The cold isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF and Li3InCl6 material. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The solid electrolyte provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 65% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%.
