Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.3 MPa or more. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. A 3 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 600 to 750 degrees C. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 1.5 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The anode support contains nickel oxide and scandia-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The reversible cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 3 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Zirconium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%.

title: nickel sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, carbon nanotubes, and carboxymethyl cellulose is described. A lithium-sulfur battery with the nickel sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The carbon nanotubes framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of nickel sulfide. The nickel sulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing nickel sulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the nickel sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using tetrahydrofuran and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The resulting LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for hydrogen with improved response time
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a gold electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the hydrogen concentration. The limiting current is proportional to the hydrogen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The ceramic is yttria-stabilized zirconia and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C. The sensor detects hydrogen with high selectivity and a response time of 20 seconds. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting hydrogen, comprising: a ceramic body comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia; a sensing electrode comprising gold disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LLZO material. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The reversible cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 600 to 750 degrees C. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 1.5 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 200 cycles. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 15 micrometers. A 15 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 87% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 88% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl propionate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyacrylonitrile matrix, lithium hexafluorophosphate as the lithium salt, and tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether as a plasticizer. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 60 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The capacity retention of 85% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 87% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 950 degrees C to 1300 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material. The content of LiI is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In the monoclinic structure, indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The 1.2 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more.

title: sulfur positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises sulfur impregnated in ketjen black and a carbon coating on the composite. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The initial capacity of 800 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The active material sulfur is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 3 mg/cm2. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. Polysulfide dissolution from the sulfur cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising sulfur and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY IDNUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 45% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O.
