The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The content of LiI is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In the trigonal structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The viscosity of 3000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The sheet thickness is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The resulting LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In the trigonal structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 200 cycles is also described. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising sulfur, ketjen black, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the sulfur is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The roll temperature is 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The method shortens the process and improves the sinterability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 65% or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 86% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from 1,2-dimethoxyethane, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The arsenic-free antimony content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of LiI is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer.
