The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the negative electrode structure of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing the ion-conductive solid powder with the magnesium additive in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%; pressing the mixture into a layer; and placing the lithium metal layer on the layer and applying a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte powder with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method of handling the same in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte powder has a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which 1 mol% to 5 mol% of the sulfur is substituted by oxygen, the oxygen being enriched in a surface region having a thickness of 2 nm to 20 nm. The powder is prepared by mechanically milling Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower, heat-treating the milled mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in argon, and exposing the heat-treated powder to an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hour to 3 hours so that the surface region is formed by controlled hydrolysis. The P-O bonds in the surface region are stable against water vapor, so that the cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation measured in a sealed 1 L chamber after 60 minutes of exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C is 5 cm3/g or less, and the ionic conductivity retention after the exposure is 85% or more. Because the surface region is thin and lithium-ion conductive, the grain boundary resistance of a pressed pellet remains 20% or less of the total resistance. The powder can be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box and is applicable to Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO-containing composite electrolytes.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte powder comprising a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which 1 mol% to 5 mol% of sulfur is substituted by oxygen, wherein the oxygen is enriched in a surface region of the powder having a thickness of 2 nm to 20 nm, and wherein a cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation of the powder measured in a sealed chamber of 1 L after 60 minutes of exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C is 5 cm3/g or less.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with an indium additive. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 1 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia with a thickness of 8 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The stack of 100 cells can be paired with a lithium battery for load leveling. The scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 95% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The cell operates at 650 to 800 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. A 8 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The lanthanum strontium manganite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 650 to 800 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 8 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a molybdenum disulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The molybdenum disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The molybdenum disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 200 cycles is also described. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising sulfur, ketjen black, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the sulfur is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The cold isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 70% or more.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The composite shows a capacity of 800 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The molybdenum disulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The molybdenum disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; molybdenum disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The resulting Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: titanium disulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises titanium disulfide impregnated in graphene and a carbon coating on the composite. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The active material titanium disulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the titanium disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing titanium disulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the titanium disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The uniaxial pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and cycle life of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A precursor of the LLZO, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.15 <= v <= 0.5, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window and cycle life of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a lithium sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The lithium sulfide is melt-diffused into ketjen black at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The confinement of lithium sulfide in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The carbon coating on the lithium sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 3 mg/cm2.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyvinylidene fluoride binder
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The sulfur cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the sulfur cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium indium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

assignee: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a lanthanum fluoride solid electrolyte for detecting hydrogen
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 400 degrees C. The sensor detects hydrogen with high selectivity and a response time of 5 seconds. The sensor shows a response time of 5 seconds to a step change of hydrogen concentration at 400 degrees C.
