The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for hydrogen with improved response time
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting hydrogen comprises a gadolinium-doped ceria ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising gold, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The ceramic is gadolinium-doped ceria and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 400 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The multilayer structure with the gadolinium-doped ceria ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The sensor shows a response time of 20 seconds to a step change of hydrogen concentration at 400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects hydrogen.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li6PS5Cl and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7% after 100 cycles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the negative electrode structure of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing the solid electrolyte powder with the silver additive in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt%; pressing the mixture into a layer; and placing the lithium metal layer on the layer and applying a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The confinement of iron sulfide in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the iron sulfide cathode. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing iron sulfide with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the iron sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ceramic ion conductor particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The sheet thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, the porosity is 30% or less, and the conductivity is 1.4 mS/cm or more. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and carboxymethyl cellulose binder
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which nickel sulfide is confined in the pores of ketjen black to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of nickel sulfide. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the nickel sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The confinement of nickel sulfide in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 100 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The bilayer structure improves the moisture stability compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by atomic layer deposition followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive in an amount of 2 wt%. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate is also described. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a yttria-stabilized zirconia solid electrolyte for detecting hydrogen
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. The limiting current is proportional to the hydrogen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The protective layer improves the durability of the yttria-stabilized zirconia sensor in an exhaust gas.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting hydrogen, comprising: a ceramic body comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia; a sensing electrode comprising platinum disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 700 degrees C.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The capacity retention of 88% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% with the electrolyte. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. With 0.5 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and production method thereof
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 70% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites.
