The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with silica nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiBr at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises titanium disulfide impregnated in graphene and a carbon coating on the composite. Polysulfide dissolution from the titanium disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The titanium disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; titanium disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming an ion-conductive solid sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3YCl6. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The capacity retention of 85% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

assignee: University Of Selexen INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC Cooperation Foundation
title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The method prevents short circuit and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Disclosed is a UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tungsten and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 950 degrees C to 1300 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 50 micrometers. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 20 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 100 mPa s to 5000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The laminate of 4 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive in an amount of 2 wt%. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The warm isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. A precursor of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: lithium sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which lithium sulfide is confined in the pores of graphene to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The confinement of lithium sulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles is also described. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; lithium sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% to suppress dendrites. The Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The critical current density is 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved high-voltage stability and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 88% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 55% or more.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. The solid electrolyte of NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode. The multilayer structure with the NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of hydrogen concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects hydrogen.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and tin substitution for improved moisture stability
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid is a crystallized glass comprising a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix having a Li2S to P2S5 molar ratio of 75:25 in which 2 mol% to 6 mol% of the phosphorus is substituted by tin, and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated from the matrix.
