Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The resulting Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. With 1 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life and sheet formability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The cold isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 93% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: A reversible solid oxide cell with a 3 micrometer electrolyte operable in fuel cell mode and electrolysis mode at 500 to 650 degrees C is described. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. A 3 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The thin 3 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.0 W/cm2. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 500 to 650 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 96% or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing titania nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a sodium beta-alumina solid electrolyte for detecting hydrogen
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of barium carbonate that converts the hydrogen concentration into an ionic activity. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of hydrogen concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The sensor with a response time of 5 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for hydrogen. The sensor detects hydrogen with high selectivity and a response time of 5 seconds. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 700 degrees C. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for hydrogen.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising barium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects hydrogen.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using tetrahydrofuran
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The LiNbO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 30 micrometers. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LATP material. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a tungsten oxide with a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF, LLZO, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3YCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and Li3YCl6 material. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

assignee: Qilunhe New Energy Technology CO., LTD.
title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiBr, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The LGPS and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the content of LiI is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The cold isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF). The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The tensile strength is 1.2 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The content of Li2O is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. With zirconium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A precursor of the LATP and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The lithium hexafluorophosphate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
