A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate and a film-forming additive
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The 1.5 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%.

title: Method for forming a conductive polymer layer on a dielectric oxide of a solid electrolytic capacitor
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the aluminum capacitor. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The capacitor withstands 105 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The aluminum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The solid electrolyte layer covers the dielectric oxide film inside the pores of the anode body. The capacitor rated at 6.3 V may be used in a charging circuit for a lithium ion battery. The polyaniline layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 5 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a aluminum anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 6.3 V.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute Of Energy Materials
title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The low electronic conductivity of the LiF, Li3YCl6, and LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY Co., Ltd.
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved cycle life and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 1 wt%. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 2 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The roll pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell and a sensing cell on a zirconia substrate
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which carbon dioxide is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. The solid electrolyte of sodium beta-alumina conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to carbon dioxide against interfering gases. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 500 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the carbon dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The sensing electrode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting carbon dioxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising sodium beta-alumina; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, fluoroethylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The capacity retention of 92% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises iron sulfide impregnated in graphene and a carbon coating on the composite. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the iron sulfide cathode. The iron sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The iron sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 100 cycles is also described. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; iron sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an oxygen source at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: Disclosed is a thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a iron sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The cathode delivering 600 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of iron sulfide. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. The iron sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The iron sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing iron sulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the iron sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and a capacitor using the dispersion are provided. The capacitor withstands 150 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polypyrrole layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The capacitor rated at 10 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the niobium capacitor. The anode body is a sintered pellet of niobium powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. The 100 microfarad capacitor smooths the output of a lithium battery converter. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polypyrrole particles doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The iron sulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The iron sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising iron sulfide, porous carbon, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the iron sulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The cold isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate and a film-forming additive
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive in an amount of 2 wt%. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. With 2 wt% of 1,3-propane sultone, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The additive 1,3-propane sultone is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with aluminum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and an aluminum oxide with a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for producing the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: sulfur positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The carbon nanotubes framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of sulfur. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyvinylidene fluoride. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The active material sulfur is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a gadolinium-doped ceria solid electrolyte for detecting sulfur dioxide
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting sulfur dioxide comprises a gadolinium-doped ceria ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising gold, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The sensor with a response time of 10 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for sulfur dioxide. The sensor shows a response time of 10 seconds to a step change of sulfur dioxide concentration at 300 degrees C. The sensor detects sulfur dioxide with high selectivity and a response time of 10 seconds. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The ceramic is gadolinium-doped ceria and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 300 degrees C. The multilayer structure with the gadolinium-doped ceria ceramic allows mass production by co-firing.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1.
