A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The LGPS material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and LLTO material. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF, Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7P3S11. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute Of Energy Materials
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The uniaxial pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfur cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 3 mg/cm2. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising ketjen black; sulfur impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Composite cathode comprising nickel sulfide and ketjen black and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, ketjen black, and carboxymethyl cellulose is described. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising ketjen black; nickel sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 0.5 wt%. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The 1.2 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The content of Li2O is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by atomic layer deposition followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium difluorophosphate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The 1.5 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and moisture stability of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an arsenic-free antimony source at a substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 86% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a gallium oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LLZO, and LiF material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

assignee: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more.

title: iron sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The initial capacity of 800 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 4 mg/cm2. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 800 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. A separator coated with porous carbon traps the polysulfides on the cathode side.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; iron sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. With 1 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO LTD
title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described.
