The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 material. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and LiF material. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The oxygen content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 65% or more.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyacrylonitrile and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Zirconium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. With zirconium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The 1.0 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. The capacitor rated at 35 V may be used in a charging circuit for a lithium ion battery. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The naphthalenesulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 150 degrees C storage. The polyaniline layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 15 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The capacitor withstands 150 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polyaniline layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polyaniline particles doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Described is a combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The titanium disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The titanium disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing titanium disulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the titanium disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The content of P2O5 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyvinylidene fluoride binder
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 85% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The carbon nanotubes framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of titanium disulfide. The sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. Polysulfide dissolution from the titanium disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The composite shows a capacity of 800 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing titanium disulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the titanium disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The capacity retention of 85% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The carbon coating on the molybdenum disulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; molybdenum disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of a solid electrolyte cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state battery. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the sinterability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A precursor of the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. In the trigonal structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In the trigonal structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. A lithium-sulfur battery with the titanium disulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode. The carbon coating on the titanium disulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising titanium disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1030 degrees C to 1380 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The uniaxial pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity.
