The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the cycle life in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The Li3N layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the titanium disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The titanium disulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising carbon nanotubes; titanium disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor with a conductive polymer solid electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a niobium solid electrolytic capacitor with a low equivalent series resistance and a high rated voltage. The capacitor rated at 35 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 150 degrees C storage. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The equivalent series resistance is 15 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The capacitor rated at 35 V may be used in a charging circuit for a lithium ion battery. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. A solid electrolyte of polypyrrole replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a niobium anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 35 V.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 94%. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 86% or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 87% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The resulting Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 65% or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1.
