The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 88% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The LATP, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability and cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. With 3 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% with the electrolyte. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 3 wt%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The resulting Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Described is a combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The additive 1,3-propane sultone reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The combination of 1,3-propane sultone and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyethylene oxide and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 40% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state battery including the sheet are described. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved moisture stability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The uniaxial pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 65% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The LLTO and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C.

assignee: DRIOSTUS ADVANCED MATERIALS TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation for lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering.
