The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing 1,3-propane sultone as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, 1,3-propane sultone, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The additive 1,3-propane sultone is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyethylene oxide matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm.

title: semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 100 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. With hafnium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Al2O3 is described. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 88% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The viscosity of 3000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 300 mPa s to 15000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 20 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a zinc additive. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LGPS material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described. The capacity retention of 85% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. With tin substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. With 3 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state battery. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a gadolinium-doped ceria solid electrolyte for detecting hydrogen
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of lithium carbonate that converts the hydrogen concentration into an ionic activity. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 500 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the hydrogen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The sensing electrode comprises platinum and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects hydrogen.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved sinterability and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises sulfur impregnated in carbon nanotubes and a carbon coating on the composite. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the sulfur cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. The active material sulfur is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The confinement of sulfur in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising carbon nanotubes; sulfur impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The critical current density is 1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The silicon substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 2 mg/cm2. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and a silicon source at a substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V.
