The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Composite cathode comprising iron sulfide and ketjen black and lithium secondary battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The iron sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising iron sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 15 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The solid electrolyte of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte of 96% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 500 to 650 degrees C. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 500 to 650 degrees C. The cell operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a power density of 1.0 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell, comprising: tape casting an electrolyte green sheet comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite; laminating the green sheet on an anode support green body; co-sintering the laminate at 1300 to 1400 degrees C; and forming a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite on the sintered electrolyte.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a niobium oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. Polysulfide dissolution from the lithium sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 87% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%.

title: Zirconium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V and method for producing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A precursor of the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.045 or less. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The lithium hexafluorophosphate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state battery including the sheet are described. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved moisture stability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The LLTO, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The roll pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. With tin substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and LiF material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte of 97% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. A 3 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 600 to 750 degrees C. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 1.5 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The anode support contains nickel oxide and scandia-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The reversible cell with a scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 3 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a lithium sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiBr at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The resulting LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an oxygen source at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1.
