The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.2 <= a <= 2, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiBr at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium bis(oxalato)borate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tantalum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 93% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved dendrite suppression and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The low electronic conductivity of the Li2ZrO3 and LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a niobium oxide with a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 80 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The LiF and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The composite shows a capacity of 800 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The molybdenum disulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The molybdenum disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; molybdenum disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The total ionic conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 200 mPa s to 10000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 15 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In the orthorhombic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A precursor of the LiF and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The additive lithium difluorophosphate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.0 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Niobium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and carboxymethyl cellulose binder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfur cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The active material is coated with a thin lithium phosphosulfide ion conductor layer so that the cathode can be used in a solid-state cell. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. Polysulfide dissolution from the sulfur cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The confinement of sulfur in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising sulfur, ketjen black, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the sulfur is 2 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The uniaxial pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 100 mPa s to 5000 mPa s.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.6 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1.
